newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases, fall seen slower on new reserve rules.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases, fall seen slower on new reserve rules.

text.p: The rouble eased on Friday as funds were still coming from the government bond market and dealers said modified reserve requirements for commercial banks could affect the market at some stage.
The central bank is adjusting its reserve requirements from November 1, lowering requirements on some rouble accounts and raising those on foreign currency.

Banks would now cut their dollar liabilities and increase their rouble portfolio to reduce payments to the central bank under the new requirements, Aljba Alliance Bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said.
"Supporting the rouble might be a heavy burden for the central bank and it is trying to make banks join that process," Slobodnik said.
"But what the market is more sensitive for is the broader spread of the central bank's rates," he added.
The central bank said it had set 5,435/5,455 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Friday. The spread was just 10 points over the previous three weeks.
The change allows the rouble to fluctuate more on the upside.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,454-55 per dollar compared with an early 5,449-51 and 5,446-49 late on Thursday. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,454-55 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,448-50.
Overnight rouble credits yielded seven to nine percent compared with Thursday's late one to five percent.
"Rouble supply has been higher recently as investments in Treasury bills became less active after prices rose to new levels there," United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said.
"As for the new reserve requirements, the rouble/dollar market is not so fast-reacting for an impact now but in future they could make the dollar's rise slower," he added.
